ux_interpretation.primary_user: The Screening Associate, who builds the borrower profile, with the Credit Risk Reviewer who gates it and the Managing Director who carries the position after it closes
ux_interpretation.user_goal: Reach judgment sooner: spend the screening window analysing a borrower rather than locating, transcribing and reformatting the data about it, and then keep that underwriting work alive as the reference the position is monitored against
ux_interpretation.business_goal: Compress initial vetting from roughly three days toward the same day so term sheets are issued faster, protect the Credit Committee date from rework loops, and shorten the interval between a borrower's condition changing and the firm acting on it
ux_interpretation.main_task: Take an entity name to a signed-off, source-verifiable borrower profile, and then to a continuously monitored position whose covenant thresholds trace back to the clauses extracted at underwriting
ux_interpretation.context: Institutional deal desks working against live closing dates. Deep, sustained desktop work on large documents and financial models, on wide screens, for hours at a time. Every source is confidential and desk-walled.
ux_interpretation.entry_point: An entity name — arriving as a queue assignment for the associate, a review notification for the reviewer, or a ranked alert for the Managing Director
ux_interpretation.expected_outcome: A profile in which every figure carries the sentence it came from, defects are returned on the line they concern rather than by email, and the covenant thresholds established at underwriting become the live measure of the position
required_data: Entity resolution graph across parents, co-issuers, guarantors and sponsors
Credit agreements and their parsed page and clause structure
Extracted covenant definitions, leverage ratios, EBITDA definitions and amortisation schedules with source offsets
Vendor financial pulls with timestamps and pro-forma adjustment records
Internal precedent from CRM, document repository, SharePoint, drives and mailboxes, with permission metadata
Committed and drawn exposure per facility
Daily alternative signal feeds with refresh timestamps
Sector benchmarks and health score history
Review threads, challenge flags, sign-off and acknowledgement audit logs
business_rules: Every committed figure retains the source offset it was extracted from; a figure whose source cannot be resolved is marked unverifiable rather than displayed as ordinary
Desk separation is enforced on read: a walled precedent item may be shown to exist, with its desk and date, but never its content
Sign-off is individual, non-delegable and audited, and is blocked while any first-read figure is unverifiable or any blocking thread is open
An extracted covenant threshold carries forward as the monitoring reference; a position with no extracted threshold is reported as not measurable, never as comfortable
The attention band is capped at five items on both surfaces; a sixth displaces the weakest rather than lengthening the list
An acknowledgement records that a signal was seen and retains its reason; it never deletes the signal
A score computed from stale feeds must state its computation time; stale data is never presented as current
constraints: Single-tenant deployment inside the firm's own cloud perimeter, with no user prompt, search history or ingested document leaving it
Role-based access control must keep Private Equity deal notes invisible to Liquid Strategies unless explicitly permitted, since the failure mode is a compliance breach rather than a defect
Credit agreements routinely exceed three hundred pages, so extraction must stream and be partially useful rather than complete-or-nothing
WCAG AA across both surfaces; risk severity may never be carried by colour alone
Desktop-first, but every page must remain usable down to phone width, because a Managing Director will open a link on a phone even though no participant described that as their working surface.
dependencies: CRM, SharePoint, drive and mailbox connectors with permission metadata

primary_journey: Associate opens the screening queue and sees the assigned profile with its remaining window and any blocking input
Associate searches the entity and reads what the firm already knows, attaching the relevant precedent to the profile
Associate uploads the credit agreement, reconciles extracted terms against their source passages, and commits them
Committed terms populate the profile model, so the associate begins on leverage and thesis rather than transcription
Associate reviews challenge flags raised on recurring add-backs and unadjusted vendor pulls, and submits for review
Reviewer opens on total leverage, then liquidity runway, then structure and guarantees, verifying each figure against its source in place
Reviewer adjudicates challenge flags and returns any defect as a thread on the figure it concerns, then signs off
The covenant thresholds extracted at underwriting become the live monitoring reference for the booked position
Managing Director receives a ranked alert carrying the issue, the exposure and the distance to breach, and acknowledges or escalates
supporting_tasks: Chase an outstanding sponsor input from the queue without opening the profile
Request access to a desk-walled precedent item
Resolve a term defined differently by two documents
Confirm the corporate structure and guarantee package separately from profile sign-off
Adjust alert sensitivity for a single position, logged
error_scenarios: A scanned agreement has no text layer, so extraction returns nothing and manual entry must remain available with source attachment intact
A vendor feed fails mid-build, so affected figures show their last known value and its date rather than a zero
A source clause cannot be resolved at review time, making a first-read figure unverifiable and blocking sign-off
The scoring pipeline is unavailable, so the last computed scores render with their computation time stated and a stale banner
Two reviewers open the same profile, and only one sign-off may be recorded
A position booked before the platform existed has no extracted threshold and reports as not measurable

design_system_gaps.need: A control that renders a source excerpt with its citing sentence highlighted, its document, page and clause reference, and a deep link back into the agreement at that position
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A Popover carries free text anchored to a trigger. This control has a compound structured payload and two states a Popover does not model — source still resolving, and source could not be located — and the second must be visually distinct from an ordinary empty popover, because a reviewer treating an unresolved source as a missing one is exactly the trust failure this direction exists to prevent.

design_system_gaps.need: A meter expressing signed distance to a fixed threshold that can be approached from either side and crossed
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A ProgressIndicator models monotonic progress toward completion, where the end of the track is the goal. Covenant headroom has a fixed marker mid-track that represents failure rather than completion, values that continue past it, and a distinct fifth state for no current data that must never render as zero headroom.

design_system_gaps.need: A flag that carries an assertion requiring adjudication, holding its evidence and recording an accept or dismiss decision against the profile
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A Badge is a static status label with no interaction contract. This carries evidence, an adjudication decision, the deciding user and a reason, all of which become part of the profile's audit record — it has a lifecycle rather than a value.

design_system_gaps.need: A two-column reconciliation row pairing an extracted value with its source excerpt, an editable override and an extraction-confidence indicator, acceptable in place
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A List item renders content in one direction. This is a reconciliation control between what was extracted and what will be committed, holding two competing values at once with an accept action that resolves them, plus a not-found state where there is no extracted value to reconcile against.

design_system_gaps.need: An accessible text-equivalent structure for the corporate-structure canvas and the relationship map
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: The baseline offers no pattern for a graph that must be equally navigable as a keyboard tree and as a screen-reader outline. Both views are specified here per page, but the pattern belongs in the design system rather than being re-derived on each surface that renders a graph.

assumptions: No design system was supplied for this project, so Stage 4 falls back to the documented Material 3 baseline token set — colour roles, typescale, shape-corner scale, elevation levels and the 4dp spacing grid. Every value in these specs is a token name; if the firm has an existing library, this stage should be re-run against it and the token names remapped, which will change nothing structural.

Material 3 is a baseline, not a recommendation. For an institutional credit tool an information-dense system with a stronger data-table and financial-numeral treatment would likely serve better, and the baseline's default density is looser than these screens want.

A native mobile surface was specified and then deliberately cut at reviewer revision. No participant described using a phone, and the only participant who raised security described a single-tenant private cloud with no data leaving the perimeter — carrying the monitored book on a device conflicted with that requirement and had no evidence supporting it. The Managing Director's need for an actionable alert is served on the web surface, which remains usable at phone width.

Because the mobile family was cut, the Managing Director's away-from-desk case is unaddressed by design rather than by oversight. If research later establishes that need, it should re-enter at the direction fork rather than be retrofitted onto these pages.

The attention band cap of five follows from the Managing Director's objection to fifty flashing lights, but the specific number is an inference. No participant was asked how many items they would tolerate.

Page count reflects the composite A+B+C direction selected by the reviewer. HMW 1 (firm memory) is served by 02 - Precedent Search, which brings the Entity Precedent Timeline and Inbox and Drive Ingestion features into scope alongside directions A and C.

The 1.5 sigma deviation threshold in the PRD is carried as a business input, not a validated one. Stage 1 recorded that no participant was asked what false-positive rate they would accept, and the credibility of the entire monitoring surface rests on that number.

Contrast ratios are specified as requirements against token roles rather than verified numerically, because the baseline palette's concrete values are placeholders until the firm's own palette is supplied. Every pairing named here must be re-measured once real values exist.

ux: Each of the 8 pages traces to at least one Stage-2 HMW and at least one Stage-3 feature
The primary journey covers the Stage-2 journey stages 1 through 7 without introducing a step no persona described
Pages open on what each persona reads first: the reviewer's page leads with leverage, then liquidity runway, then structure, in her stated order, and buries the company overview she skips
No page requires the associate to leave the profile to verify a figure, which was the source of the reviewer's thirty-minute read
ui: Every colour reference in this artifact is a token name; the artifact contains no hex value and no rgb notation
Every component name follows the Page, Section or Component naming pattern and declares a base role from the taxonomy
Five components are declared new, each with a why_new naming what the nearest base role cannot express, and each is reused across at least two pages
All other components are declared reused, so a control that means the same thing on two pages is the same component
responsive: All 8 pages specify all four breakpoints: desktop, laptop, tablet and mobile
The responsive matrix covers the ten components whose behaviour genuinely recomposes rather than scaling
Wide content changes form rather than shrinking: the financial model becomes per-period cards, the structure canvas becomes an indented outline, the relationship map becomes a summary line
07 - Portfolio Watch becomes the attention band alone at phone width, on the reasoning that the question at that size is whether anything needs the user, not what the whole book looks like
No native mobile family is specified; the web pages carry the phone case at their mobile breakpoint
accessibility: No state anywhere is carried by colour alone; every severity, direction and status pairs its token treatment with a text label and a distinct shape
Both graph components specify a keyboard tree and a text-equivalent outline conveying the same relationships
Touch targets meet 44x44px, with at least 8dp separation and 24dp between actions of differing consequence
Data tables carry programmatic row and column header association so a cell is announced with its metric and period
Every disabled primary action announces its blocking reason programmatically rather than being silently inert
prototype: 11 flows connect all 8 pages; every from and to names a specced page
Every page is reachable from 01 - Screening Queue, the family entry
The primary journey is completable end to end in the prototype, from queue through precedent, extraction, profile and review to sign-off, and separately from portfolio watch to position detail
Return paths preserve scroll position wherever a page is entered from a list

Rendered to Figma: 8 frames at 1440x1024, 42 token variables in md.sys.color and md.sys.spacing collections, 2 component sets with 5 variants each, and all 11 prototype connections wired with 01 - Screening Queue as the starting point

pages.purpose: The associate's entry point: every profile assigned to them, what stage it is at, how much of its 72-hour window is spent, and precisely what it is blocked on — so a stalled dependency is visible on arrival instead of being discovered at the deadline.
content_structure: Global entity search bar, always available, accepting a company, sponsor or subsidiary name
Queue summary strip: profiles in flight, profiles blocked, profiles due within 24 hours
Assigned-profile list, sorted by remaining window ascending, each row carrying stage, elapsed clock and blocking reason
Outstanding-input panel listing every request awaiting a reply, its owner, and its age
Recently viewed entities
pages.navigation: Persistent left sidebar with Screening Queue, Portfolio Watch and Precedent Search. The queue is the default landing route for the associate role.
data: Assigned profile records with stage and assignment timestamp
Deal deadline and elapsed time per profile
Outstanding request records: what was asked, of whom, when
Entity name index across CRM and document repository
Recently viewed entity history for the signed-in user
interactions: Typing an entity name suggests matches from the CRM, the document repository and external vendor indexes, labelled by origin
Selecting a queue row opens the profile at the stage it was left
The clock meter exposes elapsed and remaining time as text on hover and focus, not only as a filled bar
Chasing an outstanding input re-sends the request and stamps the item without leaving the queue
Filtering to blocked is a single control, since it is the state the associate most needs to act on

states.default: Queue populated, ordered by tightest remaining window first.
states.loading: Row skeletons hold the final row height so the list does not reflow when data lands; the summary strip shows placeholder counts rather than zeros.
states.empty: No profiles assigned: an empty state naming what will appear here and offering Start new profile, distinct from the filtered-to-nothing state, which offers to clear the filter.
states.error: Queue could not load: an inline error region retaining the sidebar and search, with a retry that does not lose the active filter.
states.success: A chased request is confirmed with a toast and an immediate item state change to awaiting, timestamped.
states.disabled: Chase is disabled with a tooltip reason when a request was already re-sent within the last four hours.

responsive.desktop: Three columns: sidebar, queue list, outstanding-input panel. Queue rows show stage, clock, blocking reason and owner inline.
responsive.laptop: Sidebar collapses to icons. Queue and outstanding-input panel keep their split; row metadata drops the owner column.
responsive.tablet: Outstanding-input panel moves below the queue as a titled section rather than a side rail; two columns become one flow.
responsive.mobile: Single column. Queue rows recompose into stacked cards: entity name and clock on the first line, stage and blocking reason beneath. The summary strip becomes a horizontally scrollable chip row.

accessibility.contrast: Body text is md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface at 4.5:1 or better; secondary text uses md.sys.color.on-surface-variant, verified at 4.5:1 rather than assumed. Risk severity is never carried by colour alone — every severity state pairs its md.sys.color.error or md.sys.color.tertiary treatment with a text label and a distinct icon shape. The clock meter's tightening and overdue states change both fill token and label text.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order follows the visual column order. Every dialog and popover traps focus, returns it to the trigger on dismiss, and closes on Escape. Focus rings use md.sys.color.primary at a 3:1 minimum against both md.sys.color.surface and md.sys.color.surface-container-high, and are never removed on mouse interaction. The global search is reachable from anywhere with a documented shortcut and announces result counts to assistive technology.
accessibility.labels: Every queue row is a single labelled link naming the entity and its stage, so a screen-reader user is not read six unlabelled cells. The clock exposes an accessible value in hours remaining, not a percentage.
accessibility.touch_targets: All interactive targets are at least 44x44px with at least 8dp between adjacent targets, including the provenance affordance attached to each figure, which is a full-height row hit area rather than a small inline icon.
accessibility.reading_order: Search, then summary, then queue, then outstanding inputs. The sidebar is a landmark navigation region skippable by a visible skip link.
accessibility.status_messages: The queue count and filter results live in a polite live region, so 'Showing 14 of 31 profiles' is announced when a filter changes rather than only reflected in the strip. Retry outcomes after a load failure are assertive; SLA-window changes that arrive on poll are polite, since they must not interrupt a row the associate is reading.
accessibility.motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion the row skeleton shimmer becomes a static placeholder block at the same height, and the SLA ring animates to its new value instantly instead of sweeping. No layout movement is used to signal an update — the count and the row's own state carry it.

data_dependencies: Entity index across CRM, repository and vendor feeds
permissions: Associate role
Read access limited to deals on the signed-in user's desk, enforced by the metadata tagging that separates desks
edge_cases: A profile whose deadline has already passed must render as overdue rather than as a negative remaining value
An entity that matches several records with the same name must disambiguate by sponsor and jurisdiction before opening
A request whose recipient has left the firm must surface as unowned rather than silently awaiting
A profile reassigned mid-build must appear in the new owner's queue without losing elapsed clock
open_questions: Should the clock pause while an input is outstanding, given the associate cannot act? Marcus and Alex describe the clock as continuing to run, but neither was asked whether it should.
Is queue ordering by tightest deadline correct, or should blocked profiles sort first?

pages.purpose: Answers the question the associate currently answers by canvassing systems by hand: has this firm touched this entity, its sponsors or its subsidiaries before, and what did we conclude. Assembles a single chronological record from the CRM, the credit document repository, SharePoint, shared drives and mailboxes, bounded by the desk-separation rules.
secondary_actions: Request access to a walled item
content_structure: Entity header with resolved identity: legal name, ultimate parent, sponsor, jurisdiction
Relationship map of the entity, its sponsors and its subsidiaries, each node marked as touched or untouched
Chronological precedent timeline: meetings, investment committee memos, prior agreements, credit decisions, each with desk, date and participants
Walled-item notice listing the count of matching records the signed-in user may not see and how to request them
Coverage indicator stating which repositories were searched and when each was last indexed
pages.navigation: Reachable from the global search on any page and from the primary sidebar. Attaching a precedent set carries the user forward into the profile.

components.name: Component / Provenance Popover
components.why_new: A Popover carries free text. This must render a compound payload — the citing sentence highlighted in its surrounding paragraph, the document name, the page and clause reference, and a deep link that opens the agreement at that position — and it owns states a Popover does not model: the source is still being resolved, and the source could not be located. It is the single most-used control in this direction and appears on every numeric figure across six pages, so it is defined once as a component rather than re-composed per page.

data: Entity resolution graph linking parents, co-issuers, guarantors and sponsors
CRM interaction records with desk and participant attribution
Investment committee memo summaries
Prior credit agreements held in the repository
Mailbox and drive index entries with permission metadata
Per-repository last-indexed timestamps
interactions: Selecting a timeline entry opens its source excerpt in the provenance popover without leaving the page
Expanding a subsidiary in the relationship map extends the timeline to include that entity rather than replacing it
A walled item shows that it exists, its desk and its date, but never its content — requesting access opens a logged request to the owning desk
Attaching a precedent set writes the selected entries into the profile so the associate never re-finds them

states.default: Timeline populated, newest first, with the relationship map showing touched nodes emphasised.
states.loading: The timeline streams in per repository, each source showing its own progress row, so a slow mailbox index does not hold back CRM results already available.
states.empty: No prior contact found: states plainly that all five repositories were searched, names them and their index dates, and offers to widen the search to sponsor and subsidiary names. This is a finding, not a failure, and is worded as one.
states.error: One or more repositories unreachable: results render from those that responded, with a persistent banner naming which source is missing so a partial answer is never mistaken for a complete one.
states.success: Attachment confirmed with a toast and a count of entries carried into the profile.
states.disabled: Attach is disabled with a stated reason until at least one entry is selected.

responsive.desktop: Two columns: relationship map fixed left, timeline scrolling right, entity header spanning both.
responsive.laptop: Map narrows and drops to a compact variant showing one generation at a time with a control to step up or down the structure.
responsive.tablet: Map moves above the timeline as a collapsible section, defaulting to collapsed so the timeline is the first content in view.
responsive.mobile: Map becomes a summary line stating the entity, its parent and the number of related entities, expandable to a full-screen view. Timeline entries stack with desk and date above the summary.

accessibility.contrast: Body text is md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface at 4.5:1 or better; secondary text uses md.sys.color.on-surface-variant, verified rather than assumed. Severity is never carried by colour alone — every md.sys.color.error treatment is paired with a text label and a distinct icon shape. Touched and untouched map nodes differ in shape and label as well as fill.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order follows visual column order. Dialogs and popovers trap focus, return it to the trigger on dismiss, and close on Escape. Focus rings use md.sys.color.primary at 3:1 minimum against md.sys.color.surface and md.sys.color.surface-container-high, never suppressed on mouse interaction. The relationship map is fully keyboard-navigable: arrow keys move between sibling nodes, Enter expands, and each node announces its name, relationship and whether the firm has touched it.
accessibility.labels: The map has a text-equivalent structure list conveying the same parent, co-issuer and guarantor relationships in reading order. Timeline entries announce as 'meeting, London Private Equity, March 2024' rather than as unlabelled dates.
accessibility.touch_targets: All interactive targets are at least 44x44px with at least 8dp separation. The provenance affordance is a full-height row hit area, not a small inline icon.
accessibility.reading_order: Entity identity, then coverage indicator, then timeline, then relationship map. The coverage indicator precedes results deliberately: a user must know what was searched before reading what was found.
accessibility.status_messages: Per-repository progress is announced politely as each source completes ('CRM returned 6 matches; mailbox index still searching'), because results arriving silently is the exact failure the page exists to fix. The unreachable-source banner is assertive — a missing repository changes what the result set means, so it must not wait for focus.
accessibility.motion: Results stream in without slide or fade under prefers-reduced-motion; the timeline appends entries directly. Progress rows use a determinate bar with a text percentage rather than an indeterminate animation.

data_dependencies: Mailbox and drive index with permission metadata
permissions: Associate role
Results filtered by the metadata tagging that keeps one desk's notes invisible to another unless explicitly permitted
edge_cases: An entity whose name matches several unrelated companies must resolve by sponsor and jurisdiction before any timeline is shown
An index older than its freshness threshold must be declared stale rather than presented as current
A precedent item whose author has left the firm must still attribute the desk
A subsidiary that changed ownership between the prior contact and now must show the relationship as historical, not current
Zero results must be distinguishable from an unreachable repository at a glance
open_questions: What is the acceptable index lag before a repository is treated as stale? No participant was asked.
Who approves a walled-item access request, and against what service level? The compliance stakeholder was not interviewed.

pages.purpose: Turns a credit agreement into structured, committable figures. Every extracted term is shown beside the sentence it came from with an extraction confidence, so the associate reconciles rather than re-types, and nothing enters the model unreviewed.
content_structure: Document rail listing every uploaded agreement and its extraction status
Extraction summary: terms found, terms needing review, terms not found
Grouped term list — covenant definitions and thresholds, leverage ratios, the EBITDA definition as written in this document, and the amortisation schedule
Source panel showing the live document with the citing passage highlighted
Conflict tray for terms that two documents define differently
pages.navigation: Entered from a profile or directly from the queue. Committing terms advances to the profile workspace with the model populated.

components.name: Component / Extracted Term Row
components.why_new: Pairs an extracted value with its source excerpt, an editable override and an extraction-confidence indicator in one row that can be accepted or corrected in place. A List item renders content; this is a two-column reconciliation control between what was extracted and what will be committed to the model.

components.name: Component / Provenance Popover
components.why_new: A Popover carries free text. This must render a compound payload — the citing sentence highlighted in its surrounding paragraph, the document name, the page and clause reference, and a deep link that opens the agreement at that position — and it owns states a Popover does not model: the source is still being resolved, and the source could not be located. It is the single most-used control in this direction and appears on every numeric figure across six pages, so it is defined once as a component rather than re-composed per page.

data: Uploaded agreement documents and their parsed page structure
Extracted term candidates with confidence and character offsets
Term taxonomy: covenant types, ratio definitions, schedule shapes
Existing committed terms for the profile, for conflict detection
interactions: Selecting a term scrolls the source panel to the citing passage and highlights it, so the eye never leaves the pairing
Correcting a value in place records both the extracted original and the analyst's override, and marks the row as accepted with an override
A term found in two documents with different values raises a conflict that must be resolved before commit rather than silently taking the first
Low-confidence and not-found terms are surfaced together as the review worklist, so the associate's attention goes where extraction was weakest
Committing writes only accepted rows, and every committed figure keeps its source offset for later provenance

Terms extracted above the commit confidence threshold can be accepted as a group, leaving individual reconciliation for the ones below it — a 300-page agreement does not require the same attention on every clause.

states.default: Terms grouped by type, review worklist pinned above, source panel showing the passage for the selected term.
states.loading: Parsing shows per-page progress with terms appearing as they are found, since a 300-page agreement takes long enough that an all-or-nothing spinner would be a blocking wait.
states.empty: No terms extracted: names the likely causes — a scanned image without a text layer, an unsupported structure — and offers manual entry with the source passage still attachable, so a failed extraction never blocks the profile.
states.error: Extraction service unavailable: uploaded documents are retained, the page states clearly that nothing has been lost, and offers retry or manual entry.
states.success: Commit confirmed with a count of committed terms and a link into the populated model.
states.disabled: Commit is disabled while any conflict is unresolved, with the disabled control naming the number of conflicts outstanding.

responsive.desktop: Three panes: document rail, term list, source panel. Selecting a term updates the source pane without scroll loss.
responsive.laptop: Document rail collapses to a dropdown; term list and source panel keep the side-by-side pairing, which is the core value of the screen.
responsive.tablet: Source panel becomes a bottom sheet that opens on term selection at half height, preserving the term list above it.
responsive.mobile: Term list is the page; selecting a term opens the source passage full-screen with a back control returning to the same scroll position.

accessibility.contrast: Body text is md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface at 4.5:1 or better; secondary text uses md.sys.color.on-surface-variant, verified rather than assumed. Severity is never carried by colour alone — every md.sys.color.error treatment is paired with a text label and a distinct icon shape. Extraction confidence is a labelled badge reading high, medium or low, never a colour alone; highlighted passages carry an underline in addition to their md.sys.color.tertiary-container fill.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order follows visual column order. Dialogs and popovers trap focus, return it to the trigger on dismiss, and close on Escape. Focus rings use md.sys.color.primary at 3:1 minimum against md.sys.color.surface and md.sys.color.surface-container-high, never suppressed on mouse interaction. Term rows are a single tab stop with arrow-key navigation between them; the source panel is reachable without traversing every row.
accessibility.labels: Each term row announces the term name, extracted value, confidence and whether it needs review. The source passage is announced as a quotation with its document and page.
accessibility.touch_targets: All interactive targets are at least 44x44px with at least 8dp separation. The provenance affordance is a full-height row hit area, not a small inline icon. Value override inputs meet the same minimum and are not smaller than the row that contains them.
accessibility.reading_order: Review worklist first, then term groups, then the source panel — the order in which the work is actually done.
accessibility.status_messages: Page-by-page parsing progress is announced politely at completion milestones, not per page, so a 300-page agreement does not flood the buffer. A term found with confidence below the commit threshold is announced with its confidence, since that is the moment the associate must decide to verify. Extraction-service failure is assertive and states that uploads are retained.
accessibility.motion: Terms appear in place rather than animating in when prefers-reduced-motion is set; the confidence meter fills without transition. The parsing indicator is a determinate percentage, never a spinner, because the wait is long enough that an unquantified one is uninformative.

data_dependencies: Document storage with page and offset addressing
permissions: Associate role
Write access to the profile's model
Document access inherited from the deal's permission set
edge_cases: A scanned agreement without a text layer must be detected and reported as such, not returned as zero terms
A term defined by reference to another clause must capture the referenced clause, not the pointer
An amended and restated agreement must supersede the original, and the supersession must be visible
A document larger than the parser's limit must be handled by segmentation rather than rejection
An override that contradicts a high-confidence extraction should be recorded but not blocked — the analyst may be right
open_questions: What extraction confidence threshold should force review? No participant was asked what error rate is tolerable.
Should a committed term auto-update if a later amendment is uploaded, or require re-confirmation?

pages.purpose: The live profile itself — the artefact that replaces the hand-built spreadsheet. Every figure is populated from committed extractions, carries its source, and can be interrogated in place. This is where the associate's analysis finally happens instead of their transcription.
content_structure: Profile header: entity, sponsor, deal size, stage, remaining window
Key metrics band — total leverage ratio, adjusted EBITDA with its add-back trail, liquidity runway across cash and revolver capacity
Financial model section with period columns and every figure provenance-linked
Adjusted EBITDA breakdown listing each add-back, its stated rationale and whether it recurs in prior periods
Attached precedent panel carrying what the firm already knew, brought forward from precedent search
Investment thesis and industry headwinds, authored by the associate
Outstanding inputs still blocking completion
pages.navigation: Reached from the queue, from extraction commit, or from search. Submitting hands off to risk review. Corporate structure and extraction are one click away and return to the same scroll position.

components.why_new: A Popover carries free text. This must render a compound payload — the citing sentence highlighted in its surrounding paragraph, the document name, the page and clause reference, and a deep link that opens the agreement at that position — and it owns states a Popover does not model: the source is still being resolved, and the source could not be located. data: Committed extracted terms with source offsets
Vendor financial pulls from Capital IQ and Bloomberg with pull timestamps
Pro-forma adjustment records for recent acquisitions
Attached precedent entries
Add-back records across prior periods for recurrence detection
Outstanding request log for this profile
interactions: Selecting any figure opens its provenance popover showing the sentence it came from, or naming the vendor pull and its timestamp where the source is a feed rather than a document
An add-back that also appears in prior periods raises a challenge flag automatically, with the prior occurrences listed as its evidence
A vendor pull not adjusted for a recent acquisition raises a challenge flag naming the acquisition and its date
Overriding a figure keeps the original visible and records who changed it and why, so the reviewer sees the adjustment rather than only its result
Submitting for review is blocked while any required input is outstanding, and the block names them
Each challenge flag states the rule that raised it and the periods it was found in, so a first-time associate learns why it matters without leaving the profile.

states.default: Model populated, metrics computed, challenge flags raised where the data warrants and nowhere else.
states.loading: Metric tiles and model rows render as skeletons at final height; committed extracted terms appear first because they are local, with vendor pulls filling in after.
states.empty: A new profile with nothing committed yet: the model shows its structure with each section naming the document or feed that would populate it, and links to extraction. An empty profile still communicates what a complete one contains.
states.error: A vendor feed failed: affected figures render as unavailable with the reason and the last known value and its date, rather than as zero or a blank cell. A missing figure is never presented as a real one.
states.success: Submission confirmed, profile moves to in-review, reviewer notified, and the associate's queue row updates.
states.disabled: Submit is disabled while inputs are outstanding or a challenge flag is unresolved; the disabled control names the specific blocker rather than saying the action is unavailable.

responsive.desktop: Model table at full period width beside a persistent right rail carrying precedent and outstanding inputs.
responsive.laptop: Right rail becomes a collapsible drawer; the model keeps all period columns, since comparing periods is the reason the table exists.
responsive.tablet: Model table gains horizontal scroll with the line-item column pinned, so a row label is never lost while scanning periods. Precedent and outstanding inputs move to tabs below.
responsive.mobile: The model recomposes from a table into per-period cards, one line item per row within each period — a wide financial table cannot be honestly shrunk, so it changes form. Metric tiles stack one per row and the thesis editor becomes full-width.

accessibility.contrast: Body text is md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface at 4.5:1 or better; secondary text uses md.sys.color.on-surface-variant, verified rather than assumed. Severity is never carried by colour alone — every md.sys.color.error treatment is paired with a text label and a distinct icon shape. Challenge flags carry an icon and the word Challenge in addition to their md.sys.color.error-container fill. Overridden figures are marked with a text superscript, not only a tint.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order follows visual column order. Dialogs and popovers trap focus, return it to the trigger on dismiss, and close on Escape. Focus rings use md.sys.color.primary at 3:1 minimum against md.sys.color.surface and md.sys.color.surface-container-high, never suppressed on mouse interaction. The model table supports standard grid navigation with arrow keys, Home and End; the provenance popover opens from the keyboard on the focused cell and returns focus to it.
accessibility.labels: Every model cell has a programmatic row and column header association, so a screen-reader user hears 'Total leverage ratio, Q3 2026, 4.2 times' rather than a bare number. Each metric tile names its unit.
accessibility.touch_targets: All interactive targets are at least 44x44px with at least 8dp separation. The provenance affordance is a full-height row hit area, not a small inline icon. Provenance affordances on table cells extend to the full cell rather than a corner icon.

accessibility.status_messages: When a vendor feed fails, the affected figures announce their unavailable state and the last-known date politely as they resolve, so a screen-reader user is not left believing a stale figure is live. Committing an extracted term announces the commit and the figure it updated.
accessibility.motion: Skeleton tiles hold final height and do not pulse under prefers-reduced-motion. Figures that update from a feed change value without a count-up animation, and the provenance popover appears without scale or slide.

data_dependencies: Committed term store with source offsets
Vendor financial feed connectors with timestamps
permissions: Associate role for edit
Reviewer and MD roles for read

edge_cases: A borrower with no prior periods cannot have recurrence detection run against it and must say so rather than reporting no recurring add-backs

open_questions: Should an unresolved challenge flag hard-block submission, or warn and record? Elena described losing trust in the whole profile, but was not asked whether she wants the system to enforce that.
What is the retention rule for override history once a deal closes?

pages.purpose: The org chart that currently costs four to five hours in PowerPoint, derived instead from the agreements. Shows the ultimate parent, co-issuers and guarantors, and marks who is actually on the hook for the debt and which subsidiaries are unrated or offshore.
content_structure: Structure canvas: ultimate parent at the root, issuers, co-issuers, guarantors and non-guarantor subsidiaries
Guarantee overlay marking which entities guarantee which obligations
Entity detail panel: jurisdiction, rating status, guarantee position, cash-flow relationship
Structural concern list — unrated offshore subsidiaries, non-guarantor entities holding material cash, entities added since the last agreement
Derivation note stating which documents the structure was built from
pages.navigation: Opened from the profile and from risk review; returns to the caller at its prior scroll position. Not a standalone destination in the sidebar.

data: Derived entity graph with parent, issuer, co-issuer and guarantor relationships

Jurisdiction and rating status per entity
Source clause offsets for each derived relationship
Prior-version structure for change detection
interactions: Selecting an entity opens its detail drawer and its derivation — the clause that establishes its role
Toggling the guarantee overlay recolours and relabels edges by obligation, with a legend that names each edge type in text
A structural concern selects and centres the entity it concerns rather than merely describing it

states.loading: The canvas draws progressively from the root outward, so the parent and first generation are readable before deep subsidiaries resolve.
states.empty: Structure could not be derived from the available documents: states which documents were searched, that no structural clauses were found in them, and offers manual construction — the reviewer must never be shown an empty canvas that implies a flat structure.

states.success: Confirmation recorded against the profile with reviewer identity and timestamp.
states.disabled: Confirm is disabled while any branch is unverified, naming the unverified entities.

responsive.desktop: Canvas fills the viewport with the concern list and entity detail as a right rail.
responsive.laptop: Canvas keeps full width; concern list collapses to a counted, expandable summary bar.
responsive.tablet: Canvas becomes pan-and-zoom with fit-to-width default; entity detail opens as a bottom sheet.
responsive.mobile: The tree recomposes into an indented, expandable outline rather than a shrunken canvas — a structure chart at phone width is unreadable as a graphic but perfectly readable as a nested list. Guarantee position becomes a labelled row on each entity.

pages.purpose: The reviewer's twenty-to-thirty-minute read, rebuilt to be a five-minute one. Opens on the three things she checks first, in her order, with every figure verifiable in place and every defect returnable on the line it concerns instead of by email.
content_structure: Review header: entity, associate, submission time, committee date and how much slack remains before it moves

First-read band in the reviewer's stated order — total leverage ratio with its adjusted EBITDA construction, then liquidity runway across cash and revolver capacity, then corporate structure and guarantee package
Challenge flags awaiting adjudication, each with its evidence attached
Open review threads and their status
Full model, collapsed by default and expandable
Company overview, collapsed by default because the reviewer skips it
pages.navigation: Reached from the reviewer's own queue and from a submission notification. Sign-off and return both exit to the reviewer queue.

Challenge flag records with evidence
Review thread history including prior returns
Committee calendar for the slack calculation
Prior profiles for the same borrower or sponsor
Reviewer sign-off log

Adjudicating a challenge flag records accept or dismiss with a reason, and the reason becomes part of the profile's record
Returning a defect posts a thread on the specific figure rather than sending a message, so a correction never becomes a round of email

states.default: First-read band populated, challenge flags listed, model collapsed, overview collapsed.
states.loading: The first-read band resolves before the full model loads, so the reviewer can begin the read she always begins with while the rest arrives.
states.empty: A profile submitted with no challenge flags and no open threads: says so explicitly and states what was checked to reach that conclusion, so an empty flag list reads as a clean profile rather than as a check that did not run.
states.error: A figure's source cannot be resolved: that figure is marked unverifiable with the reason, and sign-off treats unverifiable figures in the first-read band as blocking. The reviewer's trust problem is not solved by hiding a broken link.
states.success: Sign-off recorded, associate notified, committee packet marked ready.
states.disabled: Sign off is disabled while any first-read figure is unverifiable, and the disabled control states which figure and what would enable it — not merely that it is unavailable.

responsive.desktop: First-read band across the top at full width, threads in a right rail, model below.
responsive.laptop: Threads rail collapses to a counted drawer; the first-read band keeps its three-across layout.
responsive.tablet: First-read band stacks to a single column in the reviewer's stated order; threads become a tab beside the model.
responsive.mobile: Single column throughout. The first-read band becomes three full-width cards in order, each expandable to its source. Threads are a badge-counted section that opens full-screen. The reviewer described wanting a dashboard rather than a document, and at phone width that means a prioritised stack, not a shrunken grid.

The first-read band is reachable in three tab stops. Provenance opens and closes without leaving the keyboard, and the sign-off control announces its blocking reason when disabled rather than being silently inert.

accessibility.motion: The band does not animate into place; it renders when ready. Under prefers-reduced-motion the sign-off confirmation is a static state change with a text result rather than a transition.

Associate role for read and reply

pages.purpose: The Managing Director's standing view of booked positions, ranked by what deserves attention today. Replaces the quarterly spreadsheet cycle with a continuous measure, and answers the objection to fifty flashing lights by ranking rather than flagging.
secondary_actions: Adjust scoring sensitivity for all positions
content_structure: Attention band: at most five positions the system asserts are worth the MD's time today, each with its reason in one sentence
Exposure summary: total committed, drawn, and the share sitting in positions currently narrowing toward a covenant
Position table with health score, direction of travel, covenant headroom and direct exposure
Signal provenance rail naming which alternative signals moved and when they were last refreshed
Recently acknowledged items, so an acknowledgement is auditable rather than a dismissal
pages.navigation: A primary sidebar destination and the default landing route for the MD role. Positions open into detail and return to the same scroll position.

components.name: Component / Covenant Headroom Meter
components.why_new: A ProgressIndicator models progress toward completion. This models signed distance to a threshold that can be approached from either side and crossed, where the breach point is a fixed marker rather than the end of the track, and where 'no current data' is a meaningful fifth state distinct from zero headroom.

data: Booked position records with committed and drawn exposure
Covenant thresholds carried forward from underwriting extraction
Daily alternative signal feeds with per-feed refresh timestamps
Sector benchmarks for deviation scoring
Health score history per position
Acknowledgement log
interactions: The attention band is capped at five items by design — the constraint is the product, and a sixth item displaces the weakest rather than extending the list
Each attention item states what changed, the firm's direct exposure and the current distance to the covenant threshold, which is the three-part payload the MD specified
Selecting a position opens detail; acknowledging records that the MD saw it, with the reason retained rather than dismissed
Covenant headroom is shown as signed distance to threshold, so approaching from a comfortable position and sitting just inside a breach are visibly different
Signal freshness is always on screen, because a score computed from stale feeds is worse than no score

states.default: Attention band populated, positions ranked by score deterioration, exposure summary current.
states.loading: Attention band and exposure summary resolve first from cached scores; the full position table streams, since the MD's decision is usually made from the band alone.
states.empty: Nothing warrants attention today: an explicit statement that all positions are within tolerance, naming the number monitored and when signals last refreshed. Silence must be distinguishable from a system that is not running.
states.error: Scoring pipeline unavailable: the last computed scores render with their computation time stated prominently and a banner that scores are not current. A stale score presented as live is the failure that would cost this product its credibility.
states.success: Acknowledgement confirmed inline, the item moves to recently acknowledged, and the band re-ranks.
states.disabled: Acknowledge is disabled on positions outside the MD's desk, with the reason given as desk scope rather than a generic denial.

responsive.desktop: Attention band across the top, position table below at full width, signal rail on the right.
responsive.laptop: Signal rail collapses into the freshness banner; the position table drops the sector column.
responsive.tablet: Attention items become a single-column stack; the position table keeps score, headroom and exposure and moves the rest behind row expansion.
responsive.mobile: Attention band only, as full-width cards; the position table becomes a searchable list reachable by an explicit control. At phone width the MD is checking whether anything needs them, not scanning a portfolio, so the page becomes the answer to that question rather than a compressed table.

accessibility.contrast: Body text is md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface at 4.5:1 or better; secondary text uses md.sys.color.on-surface-variant, verified rather than assumed. Severity is never carried by colour alone — every md.sys.color.error treatment is paired with a text label and a distinct icon shape. Direction of travel is an arrow shape plus a text label, never a red or green fill alone — the entire value of this page rests on a distinction that must survive colour blindness. Breached positions carry a text label reading Breached.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order follows visual column order. Dialogs and popovers trap focus, return it to the trigger on dismiss, and close on Escape. Focus rings use md.sys.color.primary at 3:1 minimum against md.sys.color.surface and md.sys.color.surface-container-high, never suppressed on mouse interaction. The attention band is the first tab stop after navigation. Acknowledgement is keyboard-reachable per item without entering the position detail.
accessibility.labels: Each attention item is announced as a single sentence carrying change, exposure and headroom, so the payload is identical for a screen-reader user. Sparklines expose their trend as a text summary naming direction and period.
accessibility.touch_targets: All interactive targets are at least 44x44px with at least 8dp separation. The provenance affordance is a full-height row hit area, not a small inline icon. Acknowledge controls are full-size and separated from the row's open action by at least 8dp, since the two have very different consequences.
accessibility.reading_order: Signal freshness, then attention band, then exposure summary, then position table. Freshness precedes the scores deliberately.
accessibility.status_messages: The attention band announces its item count and the computation time of the scores it is showing, politely, on load and on refresh — a stale score presented as current is the failure this page most needs to avoid. Scoring-pipeline unavailability is assertive and names the computation time.
accessibility.motion: The position table streams without row-slide animation under prefers-reduced-motion, and rank changes update in place rather than reordering with a transition. Attention severity is carried by label and position, never by a pulsing treatment.

permissions: MD role

Acknowledgement recorded against the individual, not the desk
edge_cases: A position booked before the platform existed has no extracted covenant thresholds and must render as insufficient data rather than as comfortable headroom

Is five the right cap for the attention band? It follows from the MD's objection to fifty, but the specific number is an inference.
Who receives the alert when the MD is unavailable, and does acknowledgement transfer?

Headroom states are labelled Comfortable, Narrowing, At threshold or Breached in text alongside their token treatment. Score direction uses an arrow shape plus a worded change.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order follows visual column order. Dialogs and popovers trap focus, return it to the trigger on dismiss, and close on Escape. Focus rings use md.sys.color.primary at 3:1 minimum against md.sys.color.surface and md.sys.color.surface-container-high, never suppressed on mouse interaction. The covenant list and its provenance links are fully keyboard-operable; the escalation confirmation traps focus and requires an explicit confirm rather than defaulting to it.
accessibility.labels: The signal narrative is a single readable sentence carrying change, exposure and distance to breach, so the payload is identical in audio. Each headroom meter announces threshold, current value and signed distance with units.
accessibility.touch_targets: All interactive targets are at least 44x44px with at least 8dp separation. The provenance affordance is a full-height row hit area, not a small inline icon. The escalate control is separated from acknowledge by at least 24dp given the difference in consequence.
accessibility.reading_order: Header, then narrative, then headroom, then exposure, then history, then links back to underwriting.
accessibility.status_messages: The signal narrative and headroom announce on resolve, since they carry the decision. A covenant with no extracted threshold announces as not measurable with its reason when its row resolves — silence there would read as comfort, which is precisely the misreading the page is designed to prevent.
accessibility.motion: Score history renders as a static chart under prefers-reduced-motion with no draw-on animation, and headroom bars appear at final width. The chart's values are available as a table, so no information depends on the animated rendering.

data_dependencies: Covenant thresholds with source clause offsets
permissions: MD role for acknowledge
Workout authority for escalate
Desk-scoped position visibility
edge_cases: A covenant whose definition was amended after booking must show the amended threshold and mark the change
A signal that reversed after triggering must show the reversal rather than leaving a stale narrative
A position with multiple covenants breaching simultaneously must rank them by severity rather than listing them arbitrarily
A facility drawn to zero must not report exposure at its committed amount
An escalation raised twice for the same signal must be idempotent
open_questions: Does acknowledgement suppress the signal for a period, and if so how long? No participant was asked.
What authority is required to escalate to workout review, and does it differ by exposure size?

heuristic_review.fix: Every long operation reports determinate progress rather than a spinner — per-repository rows on 02, per-page parsing on 03, progressive derivation on 05 — and 07 states the computation time of the scores it is showing.

heuristic_review.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
heuristic_review.fix: Page names and content are in the credit vocabulary the personas use (precedent, guarantee package, distance to breach, first read), and the sitemap follows the Stage-2 journey rather than the document or entity tables underneath it.

heuristic_review.finding: Sign off was irreversible and unconfirmed. A mis-click ended a twenty-minute review, and the only recovery was administrative — the single most expensive action in the product had the least protection.
heuristic_review.fix: Added a confirmation naming the profile, the reviewer of record and the count of unverifiable figures, plus a 10-minute reversible window written to the audit trail. Spec updated on 06.

heuristic_review.finding: 'Adjust score sensitivity' on 07 tunes every position; 'Adjust alerting for this position' on 08 tunes one. The two labels gave no clue which scope applied, so an MD could damp the whole portfolio while intending to quiet one name.
heuristic_review.fix: Renamed to 'Adjust scoring sensitivity for all positions' (07) and 'Adjust alerting for this position only' (08) so the scope is in the label, not in the page you happen to be on.

heuristic_review.finding: Concurrent review was handled as an error scenario — two reviewers work in parallel and the second discovers at sign-off that only one may be recorded. The wasted review is entirely preventable and was being reported instead.
heuristic_review.fix: The profile header now shows who else has the review open, announced when the second reviewer opens it rather than when they try to sign off. Spec updated on 06.

heuristic_review.finding: 'Compare to a prior profile' navigated away and returned the reviewer to the top of the review, so she had to remember where she was in the first-read sequence — on the one page built around a fixed reading order.
heuristic_review.fix: Returning now resumes at the figure she left. Spec updated on 06.

heuristic_review.finding: Every extracted term required individual reconciliation regardless of confidence, so a 300-page agreement spent the associate's attention evenly across clauses that did and did not warrant it.
heuristic_review.fix: Added 'Accept all above confidence threshold', leaving individual reconciliation for the terms below it. The confidence figure was already specced; it now does something.

Each page carries exactly one primary action and orders content most-important-first; 06 opens on the three figures the reviewer checks first, in her order, rather than presenting the model uniformly.

heuristic_review.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors
heuristic_review.fix: Every error state names what happened and what is preserved before offering recovery — retained uploads on 03, last-known value and its date on 04, explicitly unverified branches on 05 — and none of them discards the work in progress.

heuristic_review.finding: Challenge flags asserted that an add-back warranted a question without saying which rule raised it, so an associate new to the desk learned the judgement only by asking a colleague.
heuristic_review.fix: Each flag now states the rule that raised it and the periods it was found in, in place. Spec updated on 04.
